## Spec review of US-00-01, round 3 (diff 0cbc66b..64a54b8, with the whole PR as context)

**Verdict: NOT COMPLIANT. One blocking item.** The round-2 fix took out the yarn layer around `stack.sh`. The same yarn → `/bin/sh` layer sits one level lower, around `expo run:android`, so on Linux the bundler still survives SIGTERM.

### Round-2 B1: verified fixed as asked, but not in effect
- `scripts/test-acceptance.sh:60` now starts `bash scripts/stack.sh &` directly, so STACK_PID is stack.sh itself.
- CI run 38536240209 (pull_request, head 64a54b8, API 31, success) has a `stack.log` that ends with `[stack] stopping the bundler` and `[stack] stopping the Gradle daemon`. There is no emulator line because the runner booted the emulator.
- The orphan list at job end went from 6 processes (round 2: bash, node, sh, node, java, java) to `adb` plus one `node` (pid 3135). The leftover `node` is the bundler (B1 below).
- I checked the TERM and Ctrl-C (SIGINT to the process group) paths with a small copy of the pattern. Both run the child's cleanup and wait for it.
- Locally on the fresh clone (test-runs/2026-10-14_103400, API 32): the stack log ends with all three stop lines, nothing listens on 8081 afterwards, and no `kq-emulator.*` file is left in `$TMPDIR`.

### Findings

**B1, BLOCKING: `/Users/sulo/workspace/knowledge-quiz/scripts/stack.sh:123` (cleanup at :57-61). On Linux, SIGTERM leaves the Metro bundler running even though the script prints "stopping the bundler".**
- **Cause:** `yarn expo run:android &` makes APP_PID yarn. Yarn 1 runs the binary through `/bin/sh -c`, and on Linux that is dash, which does not exec. So the tree is yarn → sh → node(expo/Metro). `pkill -P $APP_PID` reaches only `sh`, which dies without passing the signal on. The expo node is orphaned and keeps serving :8081.
- **Reproduced** in a `node:22` (Debian) container using these cleanup lines and yarn 1.22.22. After the stop, `node …/.bin/expo run:android` is still alive (PPID 1) and `curl :8081` still answers `packager-status:running`.
- **CI shows the same:** `Terminate orphan process: pid (3135) (node)`. Round 2's orphan list proves the `sh` layer exists on the runner.
- **Which promises it breaks:** the header at stack.sh:11-12 ("SIGTERM stops the bundler … nothing it started keeps running"), TC-00-01 Cleanup ("nothing of it keeps running"), and the round-2 fix's own reason at test-acceptance.sh:57-58. On a Linux developer machine the next `yarn test:acceptance` finds the stale Metro on 8081 and passes the readiness check immediately.
- **Not affected:** macOS, where `/bin/sh` is bash and execs the command, and an interactive Ctrl-C, which signals the whole group.
- **Fix:** start the binary without yarn: `node_modules/.bin/expo run:android &`. I checked this variant in the same container: expo gets SIGTERM, 8081 is closed and nothing is left. An alternative is `set -m` before the `&` and then `kill -TERM -- -"$APP_PID"`.

**N1: `/Users/sulo/workspace/knowledge-quiz/.github/workflows/acceptance.yml:54`** says the tests start the app "with `yarn stack`". They now run `bash scripts/stack.sh`, so the comment is out of date. README.md:27 says the same. It is still the script behind the documented command, which matches the technical note in substance. Fix: reword to "`yarn stack`'s script (scripts/stack.sh)".

**N2: `/Users/sulo/workspace/knowledge-quiz/scripts/test-acceptance.sh:47-50, 94`.** On a fresh clone with no Maestro (or when stack.sh stops at its tools check), dependencies are never installed. `yarn -s jest` then fails with "command not found" and writes no `unit.xml`, so "Jest still runs" does not hold locally. The exit code is still non-zero, and CI installs dependencies anyway. Fix: when `node_modules` is missing, run `yarn install --frozen-lockfile` before Jest, or accept and note it.

**N3: `/Users/sulo/workspace/knowledge-quiz/scripts/test-acceptance.sh:53`.** `adb get-state` fails with two or more devices attached ("more than one device/emulator"). The uninstall is then skipped without a word, and a stale installed app can again pass the readiness check. Fix: target the device that stack.sh will pick (`adb -s "$(adb devices | awk …)" uninstall`), or print a line when the uninstall is skipped.

**N4: PR #1 description.**
- "Changes" still says `yarn test:acceptance` runs "Jest …, the stack, then the Maestro flows". The order is now stack → Maestro → Jest.
- The og:impact block still says "from ac18d6fb7 to 993eed583" and "no CI saw them". CI run 38536240209 on the head is now green.

Not re-raised: the unused @typescript-eslint devDependencies (round 2 N2), which were refused.

### Other checks
- **Gates:** `detect-stack.sh commit|push` lists `yarn format:check`, `yarn lint`, `yarn tsc` and `yarn test`. All four pass on 64a54b8 with 100% line coverage. `bash -n` passes on both scripts.
- **Edge cases:**
  - A failing test turns the run red and the artifact is still uploaded (failed run 38531190069 uploaded `og-test-results`).
  - `if-no-files-found: error` is present (acceptance.yml:74). With Maestro missing, `unit.xml` is still published, so the artifact is not empty.
  - When tools are missing, stack.sh lists them and exits.
- **Out of scope:** nothing. The fix diff touches only `scripts/stack.sh` and `scripts/test-acceptance.sh`.
- **Constitution:** no violations in the fix diff.

### Criteria
| # | Verdict | Evidence |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | met | README.md:6-10 names `yarn stack`. TC-00-01 passed on a fresh clone locally (deps installed, emulator booted) and in CI on API 31. The SIGTERM cleanup gap is B1 and is tracked there. |
| 2 | external (MANUAL TC-00-02) | CI run 38536240209 on head 64a54b8, event pull_request: artifact `og-test-results` holds `junit/unit.xml` and `maestro/report.xml`, with testcases `TC-00-01 …` and `TC-00-03 …`. |
| 3 | met | TC-00-03 passed in CI (`report.xml`, screenshots) and locally. |
| 4 | external (MANUAL TC-00-04) | All four gates are detected and green, as listed above. |

Files: /Users/sulo/workspace/knowledge-quiz/scripts/stack.sh, /Users/sulo/workspace/knowledge-quiz/scripts/test-acceptance.sh, /Users/sulo/workspace/knowledge-quiz/.github/workflows/acceptance.yml, /Users/sulo/workspace/knowledge-quiz/README.md, /Users/sulo/workspace/knowledge-quiz/test-runs/2026-10-14_103400/
